title: How to Buy Dangote Refinery IPO Shares in Nigeria: A Step-by-Step Guide
summary: The Dangote Refinery IPO subscription window is expected to open in 2026. Here is a complete step-by-step guide on how to buy Dangote Refinery IPO shares in Nigeria, what you need to prepare, and how to do it through Bamboo.
body_markdown:
Most Nigerians who miss an IPO do not miss it because they lacked the money. They miss it because they were not ready when the window opened. The subscription period for a Nigerian IPO typically runs for a few weeks. If your brokerage account is unfunded, your CSCS details are missing, or you are waiting on documents, the offer closes before you get in.


The[Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals IPO](https://nairametrics.com/2026/02/22/dangote-refinery-shares-to-open-to-nigerians-in-5-months/) is expected to be the largest initial public offering in African capital market history. Analysts value the refinery at between $40 billion and $50 billion. Up to 10% of the company will be offered to investors, with a potential capital raise of up to $5 billion. When the subscription window opens, expected in 2026, demand will be high and the window will be short.


This guide covers every step you need to take, what each step involves, how to do it through Bamboo, and what to expect between application and allotment.


## **What You Need Before the Window Opens**


Before you can apply for any IPO on the Nigerian Exchange, including this one, three things must be in place. None of them can be set up on the day the offer opens. All of them take time. Start now.


### **A Licensed Investment or Brokerage Account**


To participate in the Dangote Refinery IPO, you need an account with a licensed broker or investment platform registered with the[Securities and Exchange Commission of Nigeria](https://sec.gov.ng/) and integrated into the NGX subscription process. This account is where your application funds will sit at the time of submission and where your allotted shares will be credited if your application is successful.


Bamboo is a licensed platform registered with the SEC Nigeria as a digital sub-broker, with access to the NGX primary market. If you do not already have an account, you can[download the Bamboo app](https://onelink.to/investbamboo) and complete onboarding in a few minutes. You will need a valid means of identification and a Bank Verification Number (BVN) to complete the process.


### **A CSCS Account**


The[Central Securities Clearing System](https://www.cscs.ng/) (CSCS) is the institution responsible for recording share ownership in Nigeria. Every investor who owns Nigerian stocks has a CSCS account, whether they know it by that name or not. Your CSCS number is how the registrar identifies you when allocating shares after the offer closes.


If you already invest in Nigerian stocks through Bamboo or any other licensed broker, your CSCS account has already been opened on your behalf. You can find your CSCS number in the Bamboo app under your account profile. If you are new to Nigerian stocks entirely, opening a Bamboo account automatically triggers the creation of a CSCS account linked to your profile. You do not need to visit the CSCS office or complete any separate paperwork.


The CSCS number is not optional. Applications submitted without a valid CSCS number cannot be processed by the registrar. Do not assume your account exists until you have confirmed the number.


### **A Funded Account**


Your application must be backed by actual funds at the time of submission. IPO applications are not binding commitments you settle later. The money must be available. When the Dangote Refinery prospectus is published, it will confirm the share price and the minimum number of units per application. You will not know the exact amount you need until then, but you can begin funding your Bamboo account now so you are not rushing when the window opens.


Dangote has confirmed that shares will be[purchased in naira](https://www.tekedia.com/dangote-refinery-set-for-public-listing-in-four-months-as-retail-investors-promised-dollar-dividend-option/) . The dollar dividend option, which allows shareholders to receive dividends in US dollars rather than naira, is a post-purchase feature, not a requirement at the point of subscription. You buy in naira. You choose your dividend currency later.


## **Understanding the Offer Before You Apply**


Knowing how to apply is only half of the preparation. Understanding what you are applying for matters equally, because it shapes how much you apply for and what to look for in the prospectus.


### **The Structure of the Offer**


The Dangote Refinery IPO involves the sale of approximately 10% of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE on the[Nigerian Exchange Group](https://ngxgroup.com/) . Three financial advisers have been appointed to manage the transaction: Stanbic IBTC Capital, which is coordinating international institutional placement; Vetiva Advisory Services, which is managing local market distribution and retail investor access; and FirstCap, which is focused on placements with Nigerian institutional investors including pension funds.


This structure matters for retail investors because it determines which channels the offer flows through. Retail participation will primarily come through platforms integrated with Vetiva’s distribution network and through NGX-connected digital brokers like Bamboo.


### **The Dollar Dividend Structure**


One of the most distinctive features of this IPO is the proposed dual-currency dividend arrangement. Dangote has stated publicly that shareholders will have the option to receive dividends in either naira or US dollars, because the refinery earns primarily in foreign currency through petroleum exports.[Projected export revenues stand at approximately $6.4 billion annually](https://www.cnbcafrica.com/media/7771856694990/dangote-refinery-ipo-in-sight-as-oil-gas-sector-leads-ngx-rally-) , largely from petrochemicals including polypropylene and fertiliser.


This arrangement is subject to final approval from the SEC Nigeria and full confirmation in the prospectus. It is not yet a guaranteed feature of the offer. However, if it is approved as structured, it would make Dangote Refinery one of the very few stocks on the NGX that allows retail investors to hold a naira-denominated equity position with dollar-denominated income, which is a significant distinction in an environment where naira depreciation remains a structural concern for savers.


### **The NNPC Stake**


The[Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) holds a 7.25% equity stake](https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-finances/2302-53163-dangote-sets-ipo-timeline-for-its-20b-nigerian-refinery-eyes-retail-investors) in the refinery. This is not being sold as part of the IPO. It is a pre-existing position taken when the refinery was under construction, and it creates an alignment of interests between the state and the company that could influence long-term policy relationships, including crude supply arrangements.

## **What Happens After You Submit Your Application**


Understanding the post-application process reduces anxiety and sets realistic expectations.


### **The Closing of the Offer**


Once the subscription window closes, no new applications are accepted. The receiving banks or agents compile all applications and pass them to the registrar appointed for the offer. The registrar for the Dangote Refinery IPO has not yet been publicly disclosed; it will be confirmed in the prospectus.


### **Allotment**


The registrar reviews all applications and allocates shares based on the rules set out in the prospectus. If the offer is oversubscribed, which occurs when total applications exceed the shares available, shares are typically distributed on a proportional basis: each applicant receives a portion of what they applied for, scaled to match the total number of shares on offer. In some offers, a ballot system is used instead, where some applicants receive their full allocation and others receive nothing.


For an offer of this scale and anticipated demand, the proportional method is more likely, but the exact mechanism will be specified in the prospectus.


### **Refunds**


If you applied for more shares than you were allotted, or if the ballot system resulted in an unsuccessful application, your unallocated funds are returned. On Bamboo, this refund is credited directly to your wallet, where it is available immediately for other investments.


### **Listing Day**


On the day the refinery’s shares begin trading on the NGX, your allotted shares will appear in your Bamboo portfolio. From that point, you can hold them as a long-term position or trade them in the secondary market like any other NGX-listed stock.

## **Common Mistakes That Cost Investors Their Allocation**


1. **Waiting for the prospectus to open your account.** Account verification and CSCS setup take time. Starting this process when the offer is already live means you may still be completing onboarding when the window closes.
2. **Not confirming your CSCS number.** Many investors assume their CSCS account exists because they once bought a stock years ago. Confirm the number in your app or with your broker before the offer opens. An unverified or incorrect CSCS number invalidates your application.
3. **Applying based on rumoured prices.** Media estimates of the Dangote Refinery share price are speculation until the prospectus is published. Applications submitted based on estimates rather than confirmed offer terms are a risk that does not need to be taken.
4. **Underfunding your account.** If the minimum subscription lot requires, for example, N500,000, and your account has N480,000 when you apply, your application will fail. Fund your account with more than the minimum to give yourself flexibility.
5. **Missing the closing date.** IPO subscription windows are firm deadlines. The offer does not extend because demand is high. Set a reminder for the offer closing date the moment the prospectus is published.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


**How do I buy Dangote Refinery IPO shares?** You need a funded investment account with a licensed broker or platform like Bamboo, a confirmed CSCS account number, and valid identification. When the prospectus is published and the subscription window opens, you apply through your broker or platform by selecting the number of units you want to purchase at the confirmed offer price and submitting payment before the closing date.


**Can I buy Dangote Refinery IPO shares on my phone?** Yes. Bamboo is a mobile-first investment platform that allows you to apply for IPOs directly from the app. Once the offer goes live on the platform, the process takes a few minutes: select the offer, enter your units, review the total, and submit.[Download the Bamboo app here.](https://onelink.to/investbamboo)


**What is the minimum amount needed to invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO?** The minimum subscription amount has not yet been confirmed. It will be published in the official prospectus. The minimum is typically expressed as a number of units or lots at the confirmed offer price. Fund your account in advance and review the prospectus when it is released to determine the exact requirement.


**Will I definitely get shares if I apply?** Not necessarily. If the offer is oversubscribed, which is anticipated, the registrar will allocate shares on a proportional or ballot basis. You may receive fewer shares than you applied for. Any unallocated funds will be refunded to your account.


**Can I receive dividends in US dollars?** Dangote has announced a dual-currency dividend structure that allows shareholders to choose between naira and US dollar dividends. This feature is subject to final SEC approval and will be confirmed in the prospectus. The shares are purchased in naira regardless of the dividend currency selected.


**What is a CSCS account and do I need one?** The Central Securities Clearing System account is the record of your share ownership in Nigeria. Every investor participating in Nigerian stock market transactions, including IPOs, must have one. If you open an account on Bamboo, your CSCS account is created automatically. Read our full guide on what CSCS is and why it matters for the Dangote IPO for a complete explanation.


**When is the Dangote Refinery IPO date?** As of April 2026, the subscription window is expected to open in 2026, following SEC approval of the prospectus and a nationwide investor roadshow. The exact date will be confirmed in the prospectus and announced by the NGX and Dangote Group. Monitor your Bamboo app for updates.
